consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué pasó en la inauguración del festival.

items.audio: She was to have sung at the opening, but she lost her voice the night before. Her friend Sara sang instead and, to everyone's surprise, she was to become a legend. By the end of the year, Sara had recorded her first song.
opciones: A friend took the place of the planned singer.
The singer refused to perform at such a small event.
The opening was moved to the end of the year.

feedback.es: «Was to have sung» indica un plan que no se cumplió: la cantante prevista perdió la voz y su amiga la sustituyó.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige por qué no llegaron a tiempo a la ceremonia.

items.audio: We set off in good time. But for the repairs on the bridge, we would have reached the hall before the ceremony began. As it was, we slipped in during the first speech, and nobody seemed to mind.
opciones: They set off later than they had planned.
Repairs on the road held them up.
The ceremony began earlier than announced.

feedback.es: «But for the repairs» equivale a «de no ser por las obras»: las obras los retrasaron, aunque salieron con tiempo.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué se sabe del alcalde.

items.audio: The mayor allegedly accepted gifts from a builder, but nobody has any proof so far. Personally, I think he is probably not to blame. In all likelihood, the council will call a meeting next week, although it may well wait for the police report.
opciones: He has admitted taking gifts from a builder.
The speaker is certain that he did nothing wrong.
He is accused of taking gifts, but nothing is proved.

feedback.es: «Allegedly» señala una acusación sin pruebas, y «probably» es cautela: quien habla no afirma que sea inocente.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué hace la persona ante la pregunta.

items.audio: Thank you for that question. Let me clarify what I meant: the plan is not free, but it is cheap, because volunteers will cover most of the work. I take your point about the cost, though, and I am willing to review the budget once we have the first results.
opciones: He says the question has nothing to do with the plan.
He explains his idea and accepts that the concern is fair.
He promises that the plan will cost nothing at all.

feedback.es: Aclara lo que quiso decir y con «I take your point» reconoce que la preocupación por el coste es razonable.

consigna.es: Lee el correo y elige qué tono usa Mia con el casero.

items.texto: Dear Mr Brown, I am writing to report that the boiler in flat 4 is leaking again. I called a plumber yesterday, but he cannot come until Friday, and the flat is very cold at night. I do not wish to complain, but this is the second leak this winter. I would be grateful if you could arrange a faster repair or, at least, send us a heater in the meantime. Thank you for your understanding. Yours sincerely, Mia
opciones: Polite, but firm about the problem
Kind, and sorry as if she were guilty
Angry, and ready to leave the flat

feedback.es: Usa fórmulas corteses («I do not wish to complain», «I would be grateful if») pero deja claro que es el segundo problema: cortés y firme.

consigna.es: Lee el texto y elige cuál es la postura de la autora sobre los uniformes.

items.texto: Some people say that school uniforms are a waste of money, and I admit that they have a point: a jacket costs far more than a T-shirt, and children grow quickly. Even so, to be honest, I would never ban them. Uniforms reduce the difference between rich and poor families, and mornings are calmer when nobody argues about what to wear. In view of this, the best solution is cheaper uniforms, not no uniforms at all.
opciones: She thinks uniforms should be banned.
She accepts some criticism but still supports uniforms.
She believes uniforms are cheap and never a problem.

feedback.es: Concede que el coste es un problema («they have a point») pero con «Even so» mantiene su apoyo y propone uniformes más baratos.

consigna.es: Lee el texto y elige por qué el alcalde dice «Mistakes were made».

items.texto: Visitors to the old market often ask why the building looks so old and damaged. The roof should have been inspected years ago, and the crack in the north wall could have been repaired before last winter. Instead, the money was spent on a new car park. The council did have the walls painted by local students, which looks lovely, but paint cannot fix the damage. Asked who was to blame, the mayor only said: «Mistakes were made.»
opciones: It blames the students who painted the walls.
It denies that anything was done badly.
It admits errors without naming anyone.

feedback.es: La pasiva sin agente («were made») permite admitir errores sin decir quién los cometió, por eso evita asumir responsabilidad.

consigna.es: Lee la actualización y elige por qué se menciona el retraso de las fotos.

items.texto: Hi all, here is a quick progress update. So far, I have completed the first two sections of the guide, and the project is on track overall, although we are slightly behind on the last section. The main obstacle has been a delay in the photos from the school. With a tight deadline, I do not think it is realistic to finish everything by Friday, so I would propose moving the deadline to Tuesday. Could you let me know by Thursday whether that works for everybody?
opciones: To justify a request for a later deadline
To complain that the school does not help
To warn that the project may be cancelled

feedback.es: Es el obstáculo principal y la razón con la que justifica pedir más plazo; el resto del proyecto va bien.

consigna.es: ¿Qué frase, por sí sola, indica que lo previsto no llegó a ocurrir?

items.texto: Ana's train was cancelled on Saturday, so she did not go to the wedding.
opciones: She was to have gone to the wedding.
She was to go to the wedding.
She had gone to the wedding.

feedback.es: «Was to have + participio» expresa un plan pasado que no se cumplió; «was to go» solo nombra el plan, sin decir si se llevó a cabo.

items.texto: The rain stopped the match, so it finished late.
opciones: Hadn't it been for the rain, the match would have finished on time.
Had not it been for the rain, the match would finish on time.
Had it not been for the rain, the match would have finished on time.

feedback.es: En la inversión formal se mueve «had» al principio y «not» va después del sujeto: «Had it not been for...».

consigna.es: Completa la frase con la opción correcta.

items.texto: We took a hundred photographs, a few of ___ I am going to share.
opciones: them
which
those

feedback.es: Tras «a few of» se usa «which» para unir las dos cláusulas; «them» dejaría dos oraciones pegadas por una coma.

consigna.es: Completa la frase con la expresión adecuada.

items.texto: The new stadium is ___ as big as the old one, so the fans are disappointed.
opciones: every bit
nowhere near
far more

feedback.es: «Nowhere near as… as» marca una gran diferencia a la baja: el estadio es mucho más pequeño, por eso los hinchas se decepcionan.

consigna.es: Elige la palabra que encaja en el mensaje.

items.texto: Stop being so ___; it's my private message!
opciones: thrifty
generous
nosy

feedback.es: «Nosy» describe a quien se mete en lo privado de otros; «thrifty» es ahorrador y «generous» no encaja con el reproche.

consigna.es: Elige el adverbio que encaja en la frase.

items.texto: The museum is ___ open until nine, but the door was locked.
opciones: supposedly
undoubtedly
fortunately

feedback.es: «Supposedly» indica lo que se dice, y el contraste con la puerta cerrada muestra que puede no ser cierto; los otros dos no encajan con «but».

consigna.es: ¿Qué significa «throw in the towel» en esta frase?

items.texto: After ten failed tries, Ana was tired and decided to throw in the towel.
opciones: try once more
ask her boss for help
give up completely

feedback.es: «Throw in the towel» es una expresión hecha que significa rendirse; por eso, tras diez intentos fallidos, deja de intentarlo.

consigna.es: Completa el mensaje con la palabra correcta.

items.texto: Tom will ___ the minutes to all attendees by Tuesday.
opciones: approve
circulate
cover

feedback.es: «Circulate» es enviar un documento a todos los destinatarios; «approve» o «cover» no encajan con «to all attendees».

consigna.es: Escribe a una tienda: tu pedido llegó roto; pide solución con cortesía y despídete.

items.respuesta: Dear Mr Lopez, I am writing to complain that the laptop I ordered last week arrived damaged. I would be grateful if you could send a replacement or refund me, because I need it for work. I look forward to hearing from you. Yours sincerely, Ana
aceptadas: Dear Ms Ortiz, I am writing to report that my order arrived broken. I would appreciate it if you could arrange a refund as soon as possible. Kind regards, Leo

feedback.es: Se espera un correo formal: «I am writing to» para abrir, una petición cortés con «I would be grateful if» y un cierre formal.

consigna.es: Un amigo propone una fiesta semanal. Discrepa con tacto y propón algo (3–4 frases).

items.respuesta: I can see why you like the idea, but I'm a bit worried about the noise. I'd have thought once a month would be fairer for everyone, wouldn't you agree? How about a quiet dinner on Fridays instead? That way we would all be happy.
aceptadas: I take your point that we need to have fun, but I am not sure a party every week is fair on the neighbours. What about a small party once a month? I think that would suit everyone.

feedback.es: Se espera discrepar con tacto («I can see why», «I'm a bit worried»), matizar la opinión y cerrar con una propuesta («How about...?»).

notes: gramatica.1: nuevo contexto (Ana/boda) para no repetir «was to have sung» del audio; la consigna pide la frase que «por sí sola» indica que el plan no se cumplió, así «was to go» (solo plan) deja de ser ambigua; distractores sin «to have».
escucha.2: la clave depende de «But for…» (las obras), sin inversión «Had…not» que filtraba gramatica.2; distractores con eco equilibrado.

lectura.2: sustituido por pasaje de estructura argumentativa (bloque 10) para repartir el banco y evitar la repetición de contrafactuales en escucha/lectura/gramática; lectura.3 y .4 con distractores más plausibles y correcta ya no la más larga.
gramatica.4: «nevertheless» se enseña desde N5 (demasiado fácil); ahora «nowhere near as… as» (bloque 14).
vocabulario.3: «under the weather» se enseña en N5; ahora «throw in the towel» (solo N7). vocabulario.2: distractores ya no sinónimos entre sí.
escritura.1: nuevo tema (tienda, pedido roto) para no copiar el correo al casero de lectura.1; rúbricas de ambas ampliadas con variantes y contracciones.
Posiciones de la correcta redistribuidas; el validador pasa.
